Japanese study on dairy and effects on hormone levels in humans.

They tested testosterone and estrogen levels of men before and after consuming a little over 1 pint of milk. They found that men had their testosterone take a kick to the balls and saw an increase in estrogen.

They also saw urinary excretion of significant amount of estrogen and it's buddies in children, women, and men. I'd guess that this means that most of the estrogen went un-utilized. But it does indicate that there's a lot of the stuff in modern milk.

nih.gov link: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/19496976 found a PDF

Pretty alarming, especially if you're a dude.. or a woman at risk for breast cancer.

As for me, i'm thinking of taking the paleo advice on this and cutting out dairy.

Correlation /= causation.

It may be causing it, but it may also be causing a reaction in the body to produce the hormones naturally. We don't know enough about this to be fearmongering yet. Until then, if you're sure you're cutting it out do try to get your dietary calcium from another source.

Yes, there is room for ambiguity and questionable science here, but it does seem rather plausible to me. I'm really interested in investigating this further. I'm having great difficulty finding much more information on this, but i did come across this link as well from Harvard: http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/2006/12.07/11-dairy.html

"Among the routes of human exposure to estrogens, we are mostly concerned about cow's milk, which contains considerable amounts of female sex hormones," Ganmaa told her audience. Dairy, she added, accounts for 60 percent to 80 percent of estrogens consumed.

...

Part of the problem seems to be milk from modern dairy farms, where cows are milked about 300 days a year. For much of that time, the cows are pregnant. The later in pregnancy a cow is, the more hormones appear in her milk.

Milk from a cow in the late stage of pregnancy contains up to 33 times as much of a signature estrogen compound (estrone sulfate) than milk from a non-pregnant cow.

But that still doesn't imply causation, it just states that dairy accounts for 60-80% of consumed estrogen.

We have no way of knowing if it's permeating from the milk, whether the milk with or without estrogen causes human secretion, or something else entirely.

My point is, we need tests done on the effects of non-estrogen laden milk.
